## Why visit

A strong brewery visit for people who enjoy tasting a producer’s range where it is made. The bar occupies industrial premises above Blackedge’s brewery, with the production area visible through windows below. Its particular appeal is the breadth of the brewery’s own cask offer, including a dark beer, rather than a parade of unrelated guest taps. Horwich takes more planning than a central Manchester walk, so treat it as a deliberate brewery excursion. It can pair with Bolton, but do not turn a five-day trip into an all-day series of bus connections unless this producer especially interests you.

## Beer

CAMRA documents up to seven Blackedge cask beers plus brewery-conditioned beers; dark beer is normally part of the selection.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** Bolton CAMRA’s cider page and October 2026 trail identify real cider here; individual flavoured products can fall outside the definition.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Locally made pork pies are documented. Do not assume summer pop-up catering runs in November.

## Plan the visit

First-floor bar reached by stairs; CAMRA reports no lift and ground-floor toilets. Distinguish this Horwich Brewery Bar from the separate Westhoughton Brewery Tap.

**Getting there:** Plan onward bus/taxi travel to Horwich; this is not beside Bolton station.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
